scope: Initial document-level selection pass: 11 memoranda from four official file-unit PDFs, dated March 1989–July 1990 (including one undated attachment). Seven are proposed for document treatment and four for annotation. This is a selective starting set, not a complete review of 1989–1992 or of the Scowcroft collection.
method: Read the official PDF’s first page for archival provenance, then inspect the selected memorandum and its final page for authorship, date, boundaries, classification, and release evidence. Editorial proposals remain subject to compiler judgment and comparison of controlling copies.

records.title: Meeting with the White House Summit Group
records.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal. A compact statement of U.S. objectives for the Paris summit: stronger monetary coordination, support for the Brady debt strategy, resistance to competing debt proposals, and an ambitious Uruguay Round. It connects exchange-rate policy, commercial-bank negotiations, and presidential bargaining.
records.evidenceNotes: The initialed three-page briefing is dated June 24; June 26 is the meeting it prepares. Its location in Latin American Files does not limit its substantive coverage to that region. The opening withdrawal inventory lists it, but the three released pages and declassification stamp are present. Page 12 still represents a withheld one-page biography. Agendas and talking points are separate attachments.
records.editorialReview: Propose the three-page briefing as one document. Route Mexico-specific material by substance while retaining the multilateral debt strategy in Volume XXX; do not mistake the old withdrawal inventory for the present release state.

records.title: The Economic Summit at Houston
records.sender: James A. Baker III and Nicholas F. Brady
records.selectionRationale: Propose alongside Scowcroft’s July 2 assessment. The joint State–Treasury paper sets negotiating objectives and anticipated G-7 positions on agriculture, Soviet and East European assistance, debt, the environment, and China lending. It provides the substantive baseline to which Scowcroft explicitly responds.
records.evidenceNotes: The eight-page document names both Baker and Brady on page 16. The withdrawal inventory describes Baker alone; the document heading supplies the fuller authorship. The release stamp and all eight document pages are present, ending with Secret on page 23. It is attached to the Houston briefing sequence in the Scowcroft chronological file.
records.editorialReview: Compare this citation copy with State and Treasury copies before final publication. The fact that it is in Scowcroft’s file does not make him an author or addressee. Coordinate regional passages with the relevant volumes.

records.title: Houston Summit: World Bank Lending to China
records.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal for the decision process on China lending. Weighs the weakening G-7 consensus, congressional restrictions, and World Bank plans, then recommends a compromise linking expanded lending to economic reform while preserving U.S. legal constraints.
records.evidenceNotes: The three-page memorandum is undated and has a typed FROM line. Lundsager’s July 1 covering memorandum (page 5) prepared it for the July 2 briefing. The approval and disapproval lines on page 8 are blank. Page 7 prints “$700 billion,” while the conclusion on page 8 and talking points on page 9 say “$700 million”; preserve and flag this discrepancy in any transcription. The document is released despite its listing on the earlier withdrawal inventory.
records.editorialReview: Retain an undated dateline and do not claim approval or dispatch. Check the China-volume boundary and any signed or annotated parallel copy before final selection. July 1 is solely the chronology sorting reference supplied by the covering memorandum.

records.title: Houston Economic Summit
records.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal. Scowcroft links economic leadership to the NATO summit, recommends conditionality for Soviet assistance without a major U.S. cash commitment, and treats agricultural reform in the Uruguay Round as Houston’s central economic opportunity. His discussion connects German unification and COCOM reform with summit bargaining.
records.evidenceNotes: The dated, initialed memorandum occupies pages 12–14. Its first page refers to the Baker–Brady paper, and the July 1 Melby cover on page 15 identifies the two-paper package. All three pages are released and the terminal marking is Confidential. These recommendations do not by themselves establish the President’s decisions or summit outcomes.
records.editorialReview: Print as a distinct NSC assessment if space permits, with the Baker–Brady paper as a substantive companion. Compare the President’s briefing-book copy and subsequent summit conversations for annotations and outcome evidence.
